info.title: Ductus API
info.description: Status, messages, drain mode and reports of a running Ductus engine. Every call but `health` needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (create one with `ductus token create`). Browsers sign in instead (`POST /session`) and send the session cookie; their changes also carry `X-Ductus: 1`.

get.summary: Alerts: open ones first, and what happened lately.
Where alerts go, and how sending has gone lately. Secrets are never shown. Operator.

post.summary:
Send a test notification to a channel now (it says it is a test). Answers 502 with the reason
when it can't be sent. Operator; logged.

get.summary: One alert and its history.

post.summary:
Acknowledge an open alert: someone is on it. No reminders until it gets worse or recovers.
Operator.

Silence an alert: nothing is sent about it (fired, worse, reminders, recovery) until the time
is up. It still shows. Works before anything fires (planned work). A silence is not a pause:
messages still wait. Operator.

get.summary: The audit log, filtered. Needs the `audit` permission.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: A user's or token's name (a user's tokens count as theirs).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: An action (`message.dismiss`) or a group of them (`message`, `user`, `session`).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Entries older than this id (the previous page's `next_before`).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Entries newer than this id, oldest first (what an export follows).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
`json` (default: a page, newest first) or `ndjson` (one entry per line, oldest first, up to
`limit`, default 10,000, at most 100,000: continue with `after` the last id). An export is
itself logged.

200.description: With `format=ndjson`: `application/x-ndjson`, one entry (as in `entries`) per line

get.summary:
Every certificate the engine connects to, as its last check saw it (read even when this
server doesn't trust them), every one it presents (`side: ours`, as loaded), and when the
engine checks next by itself.

The company-defined documentation fields and every interface's, destination's and resource's
values. Read-only: the project's files are the source of truth.

post.summary:
Check every connection the engine needs, from its server: DNS, TCP (with the address a
firewall request needs), TLS (certificate, expiry), then each system's own login; also the
alerts' mail server, webhooks and heartbeat. Never sends anything to a destination. Listening
ports aren't checked (the engine holds them). The run is kept (`/doctor/runs`), and the
certificates it saw (`/certificates`). Operator.

get.summary: The connection checks kept (the last 30), newest first. Operator.
One kept connection check's report, as `POST /doctor` returned it. Operator.
Drain mode: accepting, draining or drained, and what's still pending.

post.summary:
Start draining: stop taking new messages (MLLP listeners close, queued HTTP answers 503,
file pickup and schedules pause) and keep delivering what's stored. Operator.

delete.summary: Stop draining: take messages again. Operator.

get.summary: The engine: version, environment, uptime, drain state.

Live updates (Server-Sent Events): an `update` event with every interface's queues, health and
the drain state, sent at once and then whenever a count or a health state changes or a delivery
finishes (checked every 2 s).
Is the engine up? Needs no token (for load balancers and monitoring).

Where each destination's backlog sits: the lanes messages wait in (the ordering key's
hash), the first message of each, and which worker a failing message holds up. Only
destinations with messages waiting are listed.

parameters.name: lanes
parameters.description:
Lanes to list per destination, most waiting first (default 10, at most 1000). Lanes
whose first message is failing, and lanes no worker reads, are always listed.

get.summary:
Which interfaces a vendor, application or host touches, how, and who owns them (for a
vendor breach or a VPN/IP change). Exactly one of `vendor`, `application`, `host`.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: An address, subnet (`10.20.30.0/24`) or host name.

parameters.name: resolve
parameters.description: Look host names up in DNS (from the engine's server), so names and addresses match.

get.summary: Every interface with its state and each destination's queue.
One interface: its state, queues and what it connects.

post.summary:
Pause a destination at once: nothing is sent or retried until it's resumed (a send under way
finishes). Messages keep queueing. No reason needed; send one now or later (pausing again
with a reason adds it). Survives restarts. Operator.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Destination name (`default` for one given with `destination:`)

delete.summary: Resume a paused destination: it sends its backlog in order. Operator.

get.summary: An interface's messages, newest first, a page at a time.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only messages with this overall status.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only messages older than this id (the previous page's `next_before`).

get.summary: The signed-in user's account.

patch.summary: Change your own name and email (a directory account's come from the directory).

get.summary:
What you did yourself (and what your tokens did): the same entries, only yours. Anyone signed
in with a username and password.

post.summary: Change your own password. Your other sessions end. Works while a change is required.

get.summary: Your signed-in browsers.

delete.summary: Sign out everywhere else: every session of yours but this one ends.

get.summary: Your saved appearance (theme and custom colors), which follows you to any browser.
Your own tokens (live ones).

post.summary:
Make a token of your own, for scripts. It acts as you at most: never above your role or
permissions, and it stops working if you are disabled. Its secret is in this answer only.

delete.summary: Revoke one of your tokens (the name as listed).

post.summary:
Dismiss many messages' quarantined deliveries at once (the quarantine screen's "dismiss
selected"), in one transaction, with one reason. Operator.

Send many messages again at once (the quarantine screen's "resend selected"): as
`POST /messages/{id}/resend` for each, in one transaction. Operator.

get.summary: One message: what was received, and what each destination did with it.

post.summary:
Dismiss a message's quarantined deliveries: nobody will fix or resend them, so they leave the
quarantine (the delivery becomes `filtered`, "dismissed by NAME: reason"). Nothing is deleted:
the message and what happened to it stay, and the dismissal is in the audit log with the reason.
Works the same in the held area. Operator.

Queue a corrected copy of a message. The original stays as it was received; its quarantined
deliveries to the copy's destinations are marked replaced. The copy is a new message (new
id, so a new `meta.id`), never deduplicated, with the original's `origin`. Refused for a
destination where the original is still pending (it may be being sent right now). Operator.

Send a message again: its quarantined deliveries, or those to the destinations named
(whatever they ended as: a replay). Each goes back to pending in place and is sent next in
its lane. Pending deliveries are left alone. Operator.

get.summary:
Metrics in Prometheus's text format: messages received and delivered, retries, timings
(receipt to sent, sends, transforms, respond-mode requests, database and API calls), queue
sizes, stopped interfaces, drain state.

Who owns which interface (`about.owner`), destination (`owner` on one someone else owns) and
resources.yaml entry, and whether each owner is an account (username, email or display name,
ignoring case), a team in `owners:`, or nobody the engine knows.
The accounts that can own things (enabled ones), for choosing a new owner: name and email.

post.summary:
What moving ownership from one owner to another would change, as `ductus owners reassign
--dry-run` shows it, plus a patch to apply in the project's repository. Writes nothing: the
interfaces' files are the project's (in git), so the change is made there and deployed. Reads
the files as they are on the engine's server now.

get.summary:
What the engine listens on and connects to, with TLS in and out: the same report as
`ductus ports`.

Quarantined deliveries across this engine's interfaces (or one interface or destination),
newest message first: what needs a person. Counts per destination are in `GET /interfaces`.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description:
Only this destination's (with `interface`, that interface's; without, any interface's
destination of that name).

get.summary: Every interface's retention, expired partitions that had to stay, and the held area.

post.summary:
Confirm an interface's shorter retention, which deletes its messages past it. It's applied
at once (or when the running change finishes). Operator.

get.summary: Who is calling, and as what. Works while a password change is still required.

post.summary:
Sign a browser in with a username and password, or a token: answers with a session cookie
(`ductus_session`), which then stands in for them. Needs the `X-Ductus: 1` header. After too
many wrong passwords for one username the account refuses sign-in for a while (429).

delete.summary: Sign out: the session ends at once and the cookie is cleared.

get.summary: Live tokens, everyone's (never their secrets). Admin.

post.summary: Create a service token (it belongs to nobody). Its secret is in this answer only. Admin.

delete.summary: Revoke a token: it stops working at once. Admin.

get.summary: All users. Admin.

post.summary: Make an account with a temporary password (the person changes it at their first sign-in). Admin.

patch.summary:
Change a user's details, role, permissions, or disable them. Refused when it would leave no
admin who can sign in. Admin.

post.summary:
Give a user a new temporary password (their sessions end; they must change it when they sign
in). Admin.
Let a user who was locked out after wrong passwords try again. Admin.

action.description:
`resend` (the delivery went back to pending), `edit` (a corrected copy was queued) or
`dismiss` (a quarantined delivery was closed without sending).

by.description: The user or token that did it.

previous_status.description: The delivery before: `sent`, `filtered` or `quarantined` (none: there was none).

sent.description:
Its notifications: sent, still to send (waiting for quiet hours to end, or being retried),
and given up on.

state.description: The state then (for `recovered`: what it recovered from).

interface.description: The interface; for a certificate, its resource.

last_notified_at.description: When people were last told (or will be, once quiet hours end).

muted.description: Its interface says `alert: { mute: true }`: nothing is ever sent about it.

recovering_since.description: Fine again since then, but not for `alerts.settle` yet (it may still reopen).

silenced_until.description: Set while silenced: nothing is sent until then.

state.description:
`ok`, or what is wrong: `error`, `stalled`, `behind` (a destination), `stopped`, `silent`,
`missed` (an interface), `certificate` (expiring or expired).

summary.description: The health view's words, as of the last check.

alerts.description: Every interface and destination, open alerts first (critical, then oldest).

configured.description: `alerts:` is in ductus.yaml. Without it nothing is judged or sent.

addresses.description: The addresses let in for it: the last lookup that found some (kept when a later one fails).

checked_at.description: When it was last looked up.

error.description: Why the last lookup failed, if it did.

colors.description: The custom colors, as the UI saves them (a JSON object).

saved.description: Whether this was saved before: false means the UI may offer the browser's own choice.

actor.description: The user's or token's name when it happened.

actor_kind.description:
`user`, `token`, `system` (the engine, or someone at the server's command line) or
`anonymous` (a sign-in as a name nobody has).

detail.description: More about it, by action (never a password, token or payload).

ip.description: The address the request came from (a proxy's, if there is one).

subject.description: What it was done to: a username, a token, `interface/destination`.

via.description: `session` (the web UI), `token`, `cli` or `engine`; none for entries from before the log.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

destination.description:
Only the destination with this name in each message's interface. Without it: all quarantined
deliveries of each message.

ids.description: Message ids (at most 500), from any interfaces.

reason.description: Why. Required; kept with every dismissal and in the audit log.

destination.description:
Resend to the destination with this name in each message's interface, whatever its
delivery ended as (a replay). Without it: every destination that quarantined each message.

ids.description: Message ids (at most 500), from any interfaces.

quarantined_only.description:
Only deliveries still quarantined, even with `destination` named (what the quarantine
screen sends: a delivery someone resolved meanwhile is skipped, not replayed). Default:
true without `destination`, false with it.

resent.description: The messages sent again, by id.

skipped.description:
Ids with nothing to resend: not found, not run by this engine, a duplicate, or no
delivery that matched (pending already, or not quarantined).

alert.description: Its alert (`/alerts/{id}`), when alerts are set up.

chain_earliest.description: Whose that is, when it isn't the server certificate's (an intermediate).

chain_not_after.description: The earliest expiry in its chain (what counts).

checked_at.description: The last check; ours: now (read from memory).

days_left.description:
Whole days left (UTC dates), counted to the earliest expiry in the chain; negative once
expired.

error.description:
Why the last check failed, if it did; ours: why renewed files can't be used (the pair
loaded before is still presented).

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the server certificate, hex.

presented.description:
Ours: where it is presented (`0.0.0.0:6661 MLLP over TLS (adt)`, `client certificate to
hie.example.org:7443 (adt → hie)`).

read_at.description: When the certificate shown was read (older than `checked_at` when the last check couldn't).

side.description:
`remote` (a server the engine connects to, as its last check saw it) or `ours` (a pair
the engine presents, as it loaded it).

stage.description: The step of the countdown it is within (a warn day; 0 once expired).

state.description:
`ok`, `expiring` (within the first of `alerts.certificates.warn_days`), `expired`, or
`unknown` (never read: not checked yet, or never reachable).

trusted.description: This server trusts it (none for ours: whether senders do isn't known here).

alerting.description: A rule names `certificate` (alerts are sent about them).

certificates.description: Earliest expiry first; never read ones last.

oneOf.description: The last check of any kind.
The last check the engine ran by itself.

schedule_seconds.description: How often the engine checks by itself, in seconds; none when `doctor.schedule: off`.

rows_left.description: Messages still to move or delete (an estimate).

sent.description: Notifications in the last 7 days: sent, still to send, given up on.

webhook.description: Scheme and host only: the rest of a webhook URL is often its secret.

heartbeat.description: The heartbeat URL (scheme and host) and how often.

oneOf.description: Sent to owners in the last 7 days (each owner address is a channel of its own).

owners.description: Owners named in interface.yaml, when a rule sends to `owner`.

quiet.description: `"22:00-06:00"` and which severities wait, if set.

Check.description: The result for one thing the project connects to.

advice.description: What a failure or warning most likely means, and what to do about it.

oneOf.description: For a server that speaks TLS: the certificate it presented (or, if none could be read, why).

secret.description: The token itself: shown this once, never stored (only its hash is).

output.description: What was sent, for destinations with `save_output: true`.

latency.description: From receipt to sent, waiting in the queue included.

catch_up_s.description: Seconds to catch up at the last few minutes' rates (only while catching up).

causes.description:
Why a backlog grows: `burst` (more arriving than normal for this hour of the week),
`slow_receiver` (each send slower than normal).

oneOf.description: The last failure (a retry or a quarantine; kept across restarts).

last_sent.description: When it last delivered (kept across restarts).

normal.description: Normal for this hour of the week, learned from the hours watched (none until then).

oldest_waiting_s.description: Seconds the oldest waiting message has waited.

oneOf.description: The last few minutes (none in the engine's first half minute).

state.description:
`ok`, `behind` (past its `behind` limit), `error` (has quarantined messages), `stalled`
(messages wait, nothing finished for a minute) or `paused` (best to worst).

summary.description:
In operations' words: "behind 1,240 (oldest 12 min), catching up ~6 min; burst: 400/min
received (normal 80)".

lanes.description: The lanes with the most waiting, plus any blocked or unread one.

lanes_total.description: Lanes the interface has (`ordering.partitions`; 1 without an ordering key).

summary.description: In operations' words: "1,240 waiting in 3 of 64 lanes; worker 2 blocked by message ...".

workers_total.description: Workers each destination has (1 in the shared pool).

connector.description: Where it sends: `mllp lab.local:5000`, `http api billing /charges`, `file out`.

health.description: Its state and why: behind, stalled, errors, and how it compares with normal.

owner.description: Set when it isn't the interface's owner.

oneOf.description: Set while it's paused on purpose (nothing sent or retried until resumed).

since_start.description: Counts and timings since the engine started.

destinations.description: Dismiss only these destinations' quarantined deliveries. Without it: all of the message's.

reason.description: Why nobody will fix or resend these. Required: it is kept in the audit log.

dismissed.description:
The messages with a delivery dismissed (`previous_status` is `quarantined`; `previous_error`
is why it was).

skipped.description:
Ids with nothing to dismiss: not found, not run by this engine, or no delivery still
quarantined (someone resolved it meanwhile).

DocsEntry.description: One documented thing and the values it has.

custom.description: Values by field key, as written in `custom:`.

interface.description: The interface it belongs to; none for a resource.

missing.description: Required fields that have no value here.

DocsField.description: A field the company declared in `docs-schema.yaml`.

values.description: What an enum (or each item of a list) may be.

fields.description: In the order the file lists them.

problems.description: What `ductus validate` would reject (wrong or undeclared values, missing required ones).

interfaces.description: Only what these interfaces use (the engine's database is always checked).

mode.description:
`full` (the default: logins included) or `certificates` (DNS, TCP and the TLS handshake of
what has a certificate; nothing logs in).

timeout_ms.description: Longest wait per step, in milliseconds (default 5000, at most 60000).

stop.description: Exit the engine once drained (for an upgrade or a server move).

paused.description:
Paused destinations (`interface/destination`): they keep their messages and don't hold
the drain up.

pending.description: Deliveries still to go, over all interfaces.

since.description: When draining started, or when it finished.

waiting_for.description:
Interfaces still holding pending deliveries (a destination that's down, or a stopped
interface, keeps a drain from finishing).

destinations.description: Where the copy goes. Without it: the destinations that quarantined the original.

payload.description: The corrected message, in full (HL7 segments separated by `\r`).

id.description: The copy's id (a new message, queued at the back of its lane).

replaced.description:
Destinations whose quarantined delivery of the original is now filtered ("replaced by
edited copy N").

oneOf.description:
How this engine took over from the one before it (`systemctl reload`: an upgrade or a
project deploy); none after a plain start.

holds_interfaces.description:
False while the engine has lost the database connection that holds its interfaces:
sending, file pickup and schedules wait until it is back (receiving goes on).

others.description:
Other engines running on this database, oldest first, and the interfaces each runs.
An interface runs on one engine at a time.

resources.description:
Calls from interface code to each database and API in resources.yaml (`fetch`: URLs
called directly), since the engine started.

stopped.description: Interfaces stopped because their code ran away (their messages wait).

error.description: What went wrong, in plain words.

kind.description:
`blocked` (a message keeps failing; its worker's lanes wait), `all_blocked` (every worker
is retrying: the receiver looks down), `uneven` (one worker has most of the backlog),
`hot_lane` (one lane has most of it), `unowned` (a lane no worker reads).

share.description: Its share of the backlog (0–1), for `uneven` and `hot_lane`.

from_version.description: The version it took over from.

sending_paused_ms.description: From the old engine's stop until this one sent (receiving never stopped).

HeadInfo.description: The first message waiting in a lane: the next one its worker handles.

attempts.description: Failed attempts: above zero, its worker is retrying it and its lanes wait.

drain.description:
`accepting`, `draining` or `drained`: a load balancer can stop sending when it isn't
`accepting`.

interfaces.description: Interfaces with unfinished messages in it.

messages.description: Messages in it, finished ones included (they go when their month drops).

months.description: By month: a month is dropped once nothing in it is unfinished.

endpoints.description: Hosts and ports, listening ports, folders to look at.

incomplete.description: Interfaces that don't name every system they connect (they may be missing here).

known.description: With no hits for a vendor or application: the names that are known.

query.description: What was looked for, e.g. `vendor "Epic Systems"`.

oneOf.description: Respond mode: requests answered, how long they took in the engine, and how many failed.

store_failures.description: Couldn't be stored (the sender was told to retry).

from.description: The sending system and where its connections come from.

oneOf.description: Who may connect to the source, when it has an `allow:` list (none: anyone).
The source's TLS, when it listens with it.

timeout_ms.description: Longest the code may run without pausing.

to.description: The receiving system (destinations may name their own).

last_received.description: When something last arrived (kept across restarts).

summary.description: In operations' words: "silent: nothing received for 47 min".

oneOf.description:
A change in progress (its older messages are being moved, or deleted when past the new
retention), if any.

configured.description: What interface.yaml (or ductus.yaml) says, in days.

days.description: The retention in force: its new messages are kept this many days.

needs_confirmation.description: The waiting value deletes messages: confirm it (`POST /retention/{name}/confirm`).

waiting.description:
A configured value not applied yet: a change is running, or it's shorter and needs a
confirmation.

would_delete.description: How many messages the waiting value would delete now, when it needs a confirmation.

health.description: What it should have received (`monitor:` in interface.yaml), checked now.

retention_days.description:
Days its messages are kept, as configured (none in respond mode: it stores nothing).
`GET /retention` has changes in progress.

since_start.description: Counts since the engine started (they start at zero with it).

source.description: Where messages come from: `mllp 0.0.0.0:6661`, `http POST /orders on 0.0.0.0:8080 (queue)`.

state.description:
`running`, or `stopped` (its code ran away: its messages wait until it's fixed and the
engine restarted).

kept_for.description: Interfaces that now keep their messages longer, with messages still in it.

worker.description: None: no worker reads it (`ordering.partitions` was lowered while it had messages).

allow.description: Who may connect: the `allow:` list (`10.1.20.0/24, epic-bridge01`), or `anyone`.

oneOf.description: With a list: each host name's addresses now, and the connections refused since start.

tls.description:
`none`, or what it presents and asks for (`presents ductus-mllp, clients need a
certificate from hospital-ca`).

health.description:
As in `GET /interfaces` (an update is sent when a state changes, not as a summary's
minutes tick on).

actions.description: What people did to it (resends, edits), oldest first.

copy_of.description: An edited copy: the message it corrects.

payload.description:
The message as received (bytes that aren't UTF-8 are replaced). Absent when the caller
doesn't have the `payloads` permission (`payload_hidden` is then true), and so are the
deliveries' `output`s.

payload_hidden.description: The payload (and saved outputs) were left out: the caller may not read them.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

last_error.description: Why it was quarantined or filtered (per destination when there are several).

origin.description: Routed from another interface: the id of the message there (`GET /messages/{origin}`).

status.description:
`pending`, `sent`, `filtered`, `quarantined` or `duplicate`: the overall status (pending
until every destination is done).

name.description: What it is for, e.g. `deploy-script`; it is listed as `<you>/<name>`.

permissions.description: Defaults to none; never more than you have.

role.description: Defaults to your own role; never above it.

name.description: Who or what uses it, e.g. `ci` or `monitoring`.

permissions.description:
`payloads` and/or `audit`. None by default: a token can't read message payloads unless
it is given the permission.

password.description: A temporary password: the person must change it at their first sign-in.

interfaces.description: The interfaces it runs (respond-mode HTTP interfaces aren't claimed, so not listed).

tls.description:
For MLLP, HTTP and directories: `none`, `TLS` (the platform's trusted certificates), or
TLS with what it trusts and presents (`TLS: hie-ca trusted, client certificate
ductus-client`). Empty for SFTP (SSH) and databases.

destination.description: Set for a destination owned by someone other than its interface's owner.

owner.description: Absent for what nobody owns (listed last).

owns.description: Interfaces, and destinations owned by someone other than their interface's owner.

reach.description:
Who the owner is: `user` (an account, in `person`), `disabled` (an account that is
disabled or refused by the directory, in `person`), `several` (names more than one
account: none is chosen), `team` (in `owners:` in ductus.yaml), `address` (an email
address, not an account) or `nobody`. Absent for the unowned.

you.description: The owner is the caller (or the person whose token calls).

disabled.description: Disabled, or refused by the directory.

addresses.description:
Where alerts for this owner go; empty: nowhere (no user with that name and an email, not
in `owners:`, not an address).

password.description: The temporary password; the person must change it at their next sign-in.

reason.description: Why, once someone says (it can be added after the pause).
Why (optional: pause first, explain after; pausing again with a reason adds it).

oneOf.description: The pause (on `DELETE`: the pause that was ended; none if it wasn't paused).

connects_to.description: What it connects to (destinations and resources.yaml), by host: what a firewall request lists.

listening.description: What the engine listens on (its interfaces and the API), by port.

deliveries.description: Newest message first; a message quarantined by two destinations is listed twice.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; absent on the last page.

done_per_min.description: Messages finished per minute (sent, filtered or quarantined).

interface.description: The interface whose interface.yaml this is; absent for resources.yaml.

changed.description: Owner values that would change, over all files.

command.description: The same change made with the CLI in the project's folder.

files.description: Files that would change, each with its changed lines.

known.description: The owners there are, when nothing matched `from`.

patch.description: The whole change as a unified diff, for `git apply` in the project's repository.

refused.description:
Files with `owner: <from>` that can't be changed safely by a program (an unusual
layout): change them by hand. While any is listed, `patch` and `command` are empty.

oneOf.description: The account the new owner names, if one does.

to_reach.description: The new owner, as `reach` in `/owners` says it.

warning.description: Said when the new owner isn't an account (or names a disabled one, or several).

interfaces.description: Only these interfaces. With neither `interfaces` nor `resources`, everything moves.

Report.description: The whole report: what `ductus doctor` prints and `--report` saves.

notes.description: Lines about this machine said before the checks (on Windows: the service's account).

destinations.description:
Resend to these destinations, whatever their delivery ended as (sent and filtered too: a
replay). Without it: every destination that quarantined the message.

previous_status.description: What the delivery was before: `sent`, `filtered` or `quarantined`.

errors.description: Calls that failed (network, SQL, timeout; an HTTP error status is an answer, not a failure).

held.description:
The held area as of the last drop: messages past their retention that someone still
needs (pending for a destination, or quarantined and kept until resolved).

kept.description: Expired partitions kept at the last drop, and why.

last_drop_at.description: When expired partitions were last dropped (hourly).

SeenCertificate.description: A server's certificate as a check saw it.

chain_earliest.description: Whose that is, when it isn't the server certificate's (an intermediate).

chain_not_after.description: The earliest expiry in the chain the server presented.

error.description: Why the check failed: couldn't connect, not trusted, expired.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the server certificate (DER), hex.

subject.description: The server certificate's common name (or organisation); none if none was read.

trusted.description: This server trusts it (the system's trusted certificates).

ends_at.description:
When the session ends at the latest (it also ends when unused for too long). None when
the call came with a token instead of a session.

must_change_password.description: An admin chose this password: nothing else works until it is changed (`POST /me/password`).

name.description: The username, or the token's name.

permissions.description: What the role doesn't say: `payloads`, `audit`. Admins have both.

token.description: ...or an API token (`dux_...`), unless `auth.token_sign_in` is off.

reason.description: Why (planned work, a known outage): shown to everyone who sees the alert.

SourceAllow.description: A listener's `allow:` list and how it's doing.

entries.description: The list as written: addresses, subnets and host names.

last_refused.description: The last refused connection's address and time.

names.description: Each host name in it with what it resolves to now.

refused.description: Connections refused since the engine started (0 when this engine doesn't hold the listener).

clients_ca.description: Senders need a certificate this CA (a `certificates:` entry) issued; none: any sender.

subjects.description: And one of these subjects (none: any the CA issued).

Timing.description:
How long something took, over every time since the engine started (estimated from histogram
buckets, like Prometheus does: good to a bucket's width).

owner.description: The user it belongs to; none for a service token made by an admin.

directory_checked_at.description: A directory account: when the directory was last asked about them (sign-in or refresh).

directory_refused.description:
A directory account the directory refused at its last check (no group, disabled or gone
there): it can't sign in or act until the directory says yes again.

locked_until.description: Refused after too many wrong passwords, until then.

must_change_password.description: An admin chose the password; the next sign-in can only change it.

source.description: Where the password is checked: `local`, or a directory.

disabled.description: Disabled users can't sign in, and their sessions and tokens stop at once.

blocked_by.description: The lane whose first message it keeps retrying.
